newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady to lower, Duri allocation down.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady to lower, Duri allocation down.

text.p: Asian crude prices were steady to lower on Friday in mostly quiet trade, although Dubai paper was active as a big trader hedged July positions.

The trader was on the buy side of at least two Dubai spreads in July/August at +16 and +22 cents and two August/September spreads at +17 and +18 cents. It was also involved in other paper trades, covering Brent/Dubai and Tapis.
Traders said the trader was protecting a wet Dubai position in July.
The activity did little to shake the Dubai spreads which were mostly in line with day earlier levels.
However, the weakness of Brent pulled the Brent/Dubai tighter. July was quoted at 85/97 cents late afternoon, in from $1.00/$1.10 in Asia Thursday.

Pertamina released its June allocations, cutting Minas to 62,000 bpd from 73,000 in May. The level surprised some, who had expected a larger cut to account for expectations that Balikpapan would take Minas to feed a new 60,000 bpd crude unit due up in June.
Instead, traders were surprised at the Duri allocation, cut almost in half to around 34-35,000 bpd from 60,000 bpd in May.
The Minas market premium had firmed in recent days to ICP +30 cents from +15 cents on the recent deals because of talk the Minas allocation would be cut.
Traders said the actual allocation would take the heat out of the premium.

However, the low allocation of Duri would add the the upward trend of the market premium. The crude was assessed at +5/+10 cents over ICP ahead of the allocation and could now find sellers raising their levels to +20/25 or even higher.
